provenance.rho_pv: 50 MW/km2 central (30-86 range). Bolinger & Bolinger 2022, IEEE J. Photovoltaics, DOI 10.1109/JPHOTOV.2021.3136805: median 0.24 MW_DC/acre tracking = 59.3 MW/km2; 0.35 MW_DC/acre fixed-tilt = 86.5 MW/km2. Turkovska et al. 2024 One Earth 7:1741 harmonised median 53 MW/km2 (US). Mongird et al. 2025 use 30 MW/km2 (project area, 75% array fill), sensitivity 15-60. Lopez et al. 2023 reV use 32 MW/km2 tracking.
provenance.rho_wind: 5 MW/km2 central (4-12 range), PROJECT/SPACING area basis. Wu et al. 2026 IOP DOI 10.1088/2634-4505/ae437f: 4.0 / 4.4 / 4.9 MW/km2 via 8D-buffer, convex-hull-5D, Voronoi. Turkovska et al. 2024: median 4.6 MW/km2 (convex hull). Denholm et al. 2009 NREL: ~5 MW/km2 (pre-2009 plants). NOTE: Enevoldsen & Jacobson 2021 report ~20 MW/km2 but that is a CLUSTER-FOOTPRINT metric excluding inter-cluster spacing -- do not substitute it here. Mongird et al. 2025 assume 12-21 MW/km2 as a forward-looking technology case.
provenance.wind_direct_disturbance: 2-5% of project area is permanently disturbed (pads, roads, foundations); remainder remains farmable/grazable. Mongird et al. 2025, citing Balotari-Chiebao & Byholm 2024. Solar arrays occupy ~75% of project area (Ong et al. 2013 NREL). This is the basis for the dual-use argument.
provenance.setbacks_wind: Multipliers of TIP HEIGHT. Lopez et al. 2023, Nat. Energy 8:1034, Table 1 (2022 survey, 1,853 wind ordinances). 50th pct: structure 2.0, road/transmission/rail 1.1, property line 1.1, water 1.2. 90th pct: structure 5.0, road/rail 2.0, property line 3.0, water 10.6 (overridden to 2.0 in their extrapolation due to small sample, n=66). CAVEAT: US county ordinances -- applied to EU sites only as an analogue.
provenance.setbacks_solar: Fixed metres. Lopez et al. 2023 Table 1 (839 solar ordinances). 50th pct: structure 61, road/rail 30, property line 15, water 30. 90th pct: structure 152, road/rail 76, property line 46, water 76.
provenance.de_10h: Bavarian 10H rule: turbines >= 10x total height from residential buildings. Applies in Bavaria; other Bundeslaender differ. Federal Onshore Wind Power Act (WindBG 2022) requires larger states to designate 2% of territory for wind by 2032 (city-states 0.5%) -- use that as an independent upper bound on developable fraction. VERIFY per Bundesland.
provenance.lopez_headline: Extrapolated US-wide, setbacks cut available wind AREA to 26% (50th pct) and 13% (90th pct) of the no-setback baseline; solar to 82% and 62%. Within 5 km of transmission the wind reduction reaches 96% (solar 53%) -- directly relevant to plant-adjacent siting.
provenance.cf_degradation: Lopez et al. 2023 Fig. 6: wind capacity factor DECLINES as setbacks remove land, because the best wind sites correlate with areas where structure density inhibits development. Solar CF is ~unaffected. So land constraints degrade wind resource quality, not just quantity.
provenance.osm_layers: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (osmnx). Buildings, highways, railways, natural=water/wetland, landuse. German OSM building coverage is near complete. NOT included: slope, soil quality. For those use Copernicus DEM (slope), CORINE / CLC+ Backbone (land cover), JRC GHSL GHS-BUILT-S (built-up surface). VERIFY current product versions before building a pipeline on them.
provenance.natura2000: Natura 2000 = EU network of protected sites: Special Areas of Conservation (Habitats Directive 92/43/EEC) + Special Protection Areas (Birds Directive 2009/147/EC). AUTHORITATIVE source: EEA Natura 2000 spatial dataset (all-Europe shapefile/GeoPackage, EPSG:3035), fields SITECODE/SITENAME/SITETYPE. Point NATURA2000_PATH at it for paper-grade exclusions. OSM fallback (boundary=protected_area, filtered for Habitats/Birds Directive / FFH / Vogelschutz / protect_class 97-99) is a first-pass proxy only -- OSM Natura coverage is incomplete and tagging is inconsistent. Treated as a HARD exclusion (no buffer).
